entries.signature: export declare function erfc(x: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The complementary error function erfc(x) = 1 − erf(x), accurate in the far tail.

entries.name: erfInv
entries.signature: export declare function erfInv(p: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Inverse error function: the x with erf(x) = p, for p in [−1, 1] (±1 give ±Infinity).

entries.name: evaluatePolynomial
entries.signature: export declare function evaluatePolynomial(coefficients: Coefficients, x: number): number; ; export declare function evaluatePolynomial(coefficients: Coefficients, x: Complex): Complex;
entries.jsdocSummary: The value at `x` by Horner's rule (one multiply and one add per coefficient). A `Complex` point gives a `Complex` value.

entries.name: exp
entries.signature: export declare function exp(value: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: e^x, correctly rounded to `scale` fraction digits. `exp(0)` is exactly 1; every other result is irrational, so `rounding: 'unnecessary'` throws. Results with more than 10 000 digits (`scale` + integer digits; about x > 23 000 at small scales) throw `ResourceLimitError`. Very negative x rounds to zero (or one unit for `'up'`/`'ceiling'`).

entries.name: exponential
entries.signature: export declare function exponential(rate: number): ContinuousDistribution;
entries.jsdocSummary: Exponential distribution with `rate > 0`.

entries.name: ExponentialFit
entries.signature: export type ExponentialFit = Fit & { readonly a: number; readonly b: number; };

entries.name: exponentialRegression
entries.signature: export declare function exponentialRegression(x: Iterable<number>, y: Iterable<number>): ExponentialFit;
entries.jsdocSummary: Exponential fit `y = a * e^(b * x)`, by least squares on `ln y` against x (so large y weigh less than in a direct fit). `r2` is measured on the original y. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` unless every y is positive, plus `linearRegression`'s conditions.

entries.name: ExtrapolationConvergenceError
entries.signature: export declare class ExtrapolationConvergenceError extends ConvergenceError { /** The best value, its error estimate and the evaluations spent. */ readonly best: ExtrapolationResult; constructor(message: string, best: ExtrapolationResult); }
entries.jsdocSummary: `derivative` or `limit` missed its tolerance; `best` is the best estimate it reached.

entries.name: ExtrapolationOptions
entries.signature: export type ExtrapolationOptions = { /** First (largest) sample step (default `max(0.1, 0.001 · |x|)`). */ readonly step?: number; /** Absolute tolerance on the error estimate (default `1e-10`). */ readonly absoluteTolerance?: number; /** Relative tolerance, times `|value|` (default `1e-8`). */ readonly relativeTolerance?: number; };

entries.name: ExtrapolationResult
entries.signature: export type ExtrapolationResult = { readonly value: number; /** Estimated absolute error of `value`, from the agreement of the extrapolation tableau. */ readonly errorEstimate: number; /** Calls of `f`. */ readonly evaluations: number; };

entries.name: factorial
entries.signature: export declare function factorial(n: number): number; ; export declare function factorial(n: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: `n!`. The `number` form works up to `n = 18`; above that the result is unsafe and it throws `NumericRangeError`. The `bigint` form is capped at `n = 25_205` (results up to 100,000 digits; `ResourceLimitError`).

entries.name: fibonacci
entries.signature: export declare function fibonacci(n: number): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: The n-th Fibonacci number (`F(0) = 0`, `F(1) = 1`) by fast doubling. Always returns a `bigint`. `n` must be a non-negative safe integer at most 100_000 (`ResourceLimitError` above).

entries.name: FileSizeOptions
entries.signature: export type FileSizeOptions = { /** * `'si'` uses powers of 1000 (`kB`), `'iec'` powers of 1024 (`KiB`), `'jedec'` powers of 1024 * with the `KB`/`MB`/`GB` labels most file managers print. Default `'si'`. */ system?: 'si' | 'iec' | 'jedec'; } & FormatOptions;

entries.name: findRoot
entries.signature: export declare function findRoot(f: RealFunction, bracket: readonly [number, number], options?: RootOptions): RootResult;
entries.jsdocSummary: The root of a continuous `f` inside `bracket`, by Brent's method. `f(a)` and `f(b)` must have opposite signs (or one of them be 0). `errorEstimate` is the width of the final bracket, so `root` is within it of a sign change.

entries.name: findRoots
entries.signature: export declare function findRoots(f: RealFunction, interval: readonly [number, number], options?: FindRootsOptions): RootResult[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Every root that a sign-change scan of `interval` can see, ascending. `f` is evaluated on `samples + 1` evenly spaced points (default `samples` 100); grid points where `f` is exactly 0 are reported as they are, and each sub-interval whose ends differ in sign is refined by Brent's method. A grid point where `f` has no finite value (it returns `NaN` or `±Infinity`, or throws a `MathError`, as `sqrt(x)` does for `x < 0`) is a gap: no sub-interval that touches it is refined, and the scan goes on. The `iterations`/`evaluations` of each result count only its refinement; the scan itself costs `samples + 1` evaluations.

entries.name: FindRootsOptions
entries.signature: export type FindRootsOptions = RootOptions & { /** Number of equal sub-intervals scanned for a sign change (default 100). */ readonly samples?: number; };

entries.name: fisherF
entries.signature: export declare function fisherF(df1: number, df2: number): ContinuousDistribution;
entries.jsdocSummary: Fisher's F distribution with `df1, df2 > 0` degrees of freedom.

entries.name: ForceUnit
entries.signature: export type ForceUnit = 'N' | 'kN' | 'lbf' | 'kgf' | 'dyn';

entries.name: formatCompact
entries.signature: export declare function formatCompact(value: FormatValue, options?: CompactOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Short or long compact form: `formatCompact(1230000)` → `'1.2M'`. Default max 1 fraction digit. With `currency` it is compact money: `formatCompact(1_250_000, { currency: 'USD' })` → `'$1.3M'`.

entries.name: formatCurrency
entries.signature: export declare function formatCurrency(value: FormatValue, currency: string, options?: CurrencyOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats money. Fraction digits come from the currency (2 for USD, 0 for JPY) unless overridden: `formatCurrency(1234.5, 'EUR', { locale: 'de-DE' })` → `'1.234,50 €'`.

entries.name: formatFileSize
entries.signature: export declare function formatFileSize(bytes: number | bigint, options?: FileSizeOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Human file size: `formatFileSize(1536)` → `'1.5 kB'`. Picks the largest unit where the value is at least 1. The number part is locale-aware; the unit label is appended in English (`Intl` has no IEC units). Very large bigints lose precision beyond 2^53, which is invisible at one fraction digit. Rounding can show `'1000 kB'` for 999999 bytes; it does not promote to MB.

entries.name: formatNumber
entries.signature: export declare function formatNumber(value: FormatValue, options?: FormatOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats a number for display: `formatNumber(1234.5)` → `'1,234.5'`. Intl defaults: 0–3 fraction digits.

entries.name: FormatOptions
entries.signature: export type FormatOptions = { /** * BCP 47 locale tag. Default `'en-US'`, so output is the same on every machine * (SSR-safe). Pass `'default'` (`RUNTIME_LOCALE`) to opt in to the runtime's own * locale, what `toLocaleString()` uses with no argument; the output then depends * on the user's machine. */ locale?: string; minimumFractionDigits?: number; maximumFractionDigits?: number; useGrouping?: boolean; /** How digits beyond `maximumFractionDigits` are dropped. Default `'halfUp'`. */ rounding?: Exclude<RoundingMode, 'unnecessary'>; signDisplay?: 'auto' | 'always' | 'exceptZero' | 'negative' | 'never'; };

entries.name: formatOrdinal
entries.signature: export declare function formatOrdinal(value: DecimalInput, options?: OrdinalOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: `formatOrdinal(21)` → `'21st'`; `formatOrdinal(1000)` → `'1,000th'`. Positive integers only.

entries.name: formatPercent
entries.signature: export declare function formatPercent(fraction: FormatValue, options?: FormatOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats a FRACTION as a percent. The input is a fraction, NOT a percentage: `formatPercent(0.125)` → `'12.5%'`, while `formatPercent(12.5)` → `'1,250%'`. Default 0–2 fraction digits.

entries.name: Formatter
entries.signature: export type Formatter = { formatNumber(value: FormatValue, options?: FormatOptions): string; formatPercent(value: FormatValue, options?: FormatOptions): string; formatCompact(value: FormatValue, options?: CompactOptions): string; formatFileSize(bytes: number | bigint, options?: FileSizeOptions): string; /** Uses the bound currency. */ formatCurrency(value: FormatValue, options?: CurrencyOptions): string; /** An explicit currency overrides the bound one. */ formatCurrency(value: FormatValue, currency: string, options?: CurrencyOptions): string; };

entries.name: formatUnit
entries.signature: export declare function formatUnit(value: number, unit: Unit, options?: FormatUnitOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats `value` with its unit through `Intl.NumberFormat`: `formatUnit(5, 'km')` is `'5 km'`, and with `{ display: 'long' }` it is `'5 kilometers'`. Units Intl has no name for (`nmi`, `psi`, `rad`, `K`, ...) print as the number, a space and the symbol; `display` does not apply to them. Power, frequency, force, torque, fuel economy and data rates all take this path (`Intl` names none of them), with `hp_metric` shown as `PS` and `N*m` as `N·m`.

entries.name: FormatUnitOptions
entries.signature: export type FormatUnitOptions = { /** BCP 47 locale; defaults to the runtime's. */ locale?: string; /** `'short'` (default) → `5 km`, `'long'` → `5 kilometers`, `'narrow'` → `5km`. */ display?: 'short' | 'long' | 'narrow'; maximumFractionDigits?: number; };

entries.name: FormatValue
entries.signature: export type FormatValue = number | bigint | Decimal | string;
entries.jsdocSummary: A formattable value. A string must be a number in plain decimal syntax (`'-1234.50'`).

entries.name: FrequencyUnit
entries.signature: export type FrequencyUnit = 'Hz' | 'kHz' | 'MHz' | 'GHz' | 'rpm';

entries.name: fromBase
entries.signature: export declare function fromBase(text: string, base: number): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Reads an integer written in `base` 2 to 36 into a `bigint`: `fromBase('ff', 16)` is `255n`. An optional leading `-` or `+` is allowed and digits are case insensitive. Anything else (spaces, `_`, a `0x` prefix, a digit too large for the base, empty text) throws `NumberFormatError`.

entries.name: frustum
entries.signature: export declare function frustum(dimensions: { readonly bottomRadius: number; readonly topRadius: number; readonly height: number; }): SlantSolid;
entries.jsdocSummary: A conical frustum: a cone with its tip cut off parallel to the base.

entries.name: FuelEconomyUnit
entries.signature: export type FuelEconomyUnit = 'km/l' | 'l/100km' | 'mpg' | 'mpg_imp';

entries.name: futureValue
entries.signature: export declare function futureValue(principal: DecimalInput, rate: DecimalInput, periods: number, options?: FutureValueOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Balance after `periods`: `principal × (1 + rate)^periods`, plus each `payment` grown to the end (Excel `FV`, negated; see the module doc).

entries.name: FutureValueOptions
entries.signature: export type FutureValueOptions = AnnuityOptions & (ScaleOptions | { scale?: undefined; rounding?: undefined; });
entries.jsdocSummary: `futureValue` options: an optional payment, and `{ scale, rounding }` only together.

entries.name: gamma
entries.signature: export declare function gamma(x: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The gamma function Γ(x) for finite `x`. `Γ(n + 1) = n!`, so this is the float factorial for `n > 18`. Positive integers up to 171 are exact products; other values use Lanczos (relative error ~1e-15) with the reflection formula for `x < 0.5`. Poles (`0` and the negative integers) throw `InvalidArgumentError`; a result beyond the double range (`x` above about 171.62, or `x` within ~1e-308 of a pole) throws `NumericRangeError`. Very negative `x` whose true value is below the smallest double returns `0`.

entries.name: gammaLn
entries.signature: export declare function gammaLn(x: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Natural log of the gamma function, ln Γ(x), for x > 0 (Lanczos, g = 7, ~1e-15).

entries.name: gcd
entries.signature: export declare function gcd(a: number, b: number): number; ; export declare function gcd(a: bigint, b: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Greatest common divisor, always non-negative. `gcd(0, 0)` is `0`.

entries.name: Gender
entries.signature: export type Gender = 'masculine' | 'feminine' | 'neuter';

entries.name: IlluminanceUnit
entries.signature: export type IlluminanceUnit = 'lx' | 'fc';

entries.name: inRange
entries.signature: export declare function inRange(x: number, min: number, max: number, bounds?: Bounds): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: Is `x` inside the interval? Defaults to `[min, max)`, the usual half-open range.

entries.name: IntegerInput
entries.signature: export type IntegerInput = string | number | bigint;

entries.name: integrate
entries.signature: export declare function integrate(f: RealFunction, bounds: readonly [number, number], options?: IntegrateOptions): IntegrationResult;
entries.jsdocSummary: `∫ f(x) dx` from `bounds[0]` to `bounds[1]`, with an error estimate. Either bound may be infinite. See the module docs for the methods, the tolerance and the failure policy.

entries.name: IntegrateOptions
entries.signature: export type IntegrateOptions = { /** `'gaussKronrod'` (default, adaptive G7–K15) or `'tanhSinh'` (double-exponential, for endpoint singularities). */ readonly method?: IntegrationMethod; /** Absolute tolerance on the error estimate (default `1e-12`). */ readonly absoluteTolerance?: number; /** Relative tolerance, times `|value|` (default `1e-10`). */ readonly relativeTolerance?: number; /** Most calls of `f` before `IntegrationConvergenceError` (default 20,000). */ readonly maxEvaluations?: number; };

entries.name: IntegrationConvergenceError
entries.signature: export declare class IntegrationConvergenceError extends ConvergenceError { /** The best value, its error estimate and the evaluations spent (sign already applied for reversed bounds). */ readonly best: IntegrationResult; constructor(message: string, best: IntegrationResult); }
entries.jsdocSummary: `integrate` missed its tolerance; `best` is the best estimate it reached.

entries.name: IntegrationMethod
entries.signature: export type IntegrationMethod = 'gaussKronrod' | 'tanhSinh';

entries.name: IntegrationResult
entries.signature: export type IntegrationResult = { readonly value: number; /** Estimated absolute error of `value`. */ readonly errorEstimate: number; /** Calls of `f`. */ readonly evaluations: number; };

entries.name: internalRateOfReturn
entries.signature: export declare function internalRateOfReturn(cashFlows: readonly number[], options?: { guess?: number; tolerance?: number; }): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Internal rate of return as a JS number (the rate that makes NPV zero), like Excel `IRR`. Cash flows start at t = 0 and need at least one negative and one positive value.

entries.name: IntervalMethod
entries.signature: export type IntervalMethod = 'z' | 't';
entries.jsdocSummary: Confidence-interval method: `'z'` (normal critical value) or `'t'` (Student's t, for estimated spread).

entries.name: InvalidArgumentError
entries.signature: export declare class InvalidArgumentError extends MathError { readonly code: "ARKI_MATH_E002"; readonly remediation = "Check the argument against the documented range in the function reference."; }
entries.jsdocSummary: An argument is outside what the function accepts (reversed bounds, negative step, ...).

entries.name: inverseLerp
entries.signature: export declare function inverseLerp(start: number, end: number, x: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The `t` for which `lerp(start, end, t) === x`.

entries.name: isComplex
entries.signature: export declare function isComplex(value: unknown): value is Complex;

entries.name: isDecimal
entries.signature: export declare function isDecimal(value: unknown): value is Decimal;

entries.name: isEven
entries.signature: export declare function isEven(n: number | bigint): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: True when `n` is divisible by 2. Zero is even.

entries.name: isOdd
entries.signature: export declare function isOdd(n: number | bigint): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: True when `n` is not divisible by 2. Negative odd numbers are odd.

entries.name: isPrime
entries.signature: export declare function isPrime(n: number): boolean; ; export declare function isPrime(n: bigint): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: Exact primality test by Miller–Rabin with a fixed base set that is deterministic for every `n < 2^64`. Values below 2 are not prime. At or above 2^64 it throws `NumericRangeError` rather than guess.

entries.name: isPythagoreanTriple
entries.signature: export declare function isPythagoreanTriple(a: number, b: number, c: number): boolean; ; export declare function isPythagoreanTriple(a: bigint, b: bigint, c: bigint): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: Whether three positive integers are a Pythagorean triple, in any order (the largest is taken as the hypotenuse). Exact: `number` inputs are squared as `bigint`, so large integers are not misjudged by rounding. Non-integers and non-positive values are simply not triples.

entries.name: isRational
entries.signature: export declare function isRational(value: unknown): value is Rational;

entries.name: isRoundingMode
entries.signature: export declare function isRoundingMode(value: unknown): value is RoundingMode;

entries.name: isUnit
entries.signature: export declare function isUnit(value: string): value is Unit;
entries.jsdocSummary: True when `value` is one of the supported unit symbols (case sensitive).

entries.name: joinUnits
entries.signature: export declare function joinUnits(parts: readonly UnitPart[], to: Unit): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Adds composite parts back into one number in `to`: `joinUnits([{ unit: 'ft', value: 5 }, { unit: 'in', value: 7 }], 'in')` is `67`. Parts may come in any order and may be fractional. It reads parts the way `splitUnits` writes them: the sign of the first non-zero part applies to the whole value, so `-5 ft 7 in` is minus (5 ft + 7 in), `-67 in`. Later parts must not be negative (`InvalidArgumentError`); that would be ambiguous. The sum is exact, rounded to a double once at the end.

entries.name: KinematicViscosityUnit
entries.signature: export type KinematicViscosityUnit = 'm2/s' | 'cSt' | 'St';

entries.name: LateralSolid
entries.signature: export type LateralSolid = Solid & { readonly lateralArea: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A solid with a curved or slanted side: `lateralArea` excludes the bases.

entries.name: lcm
entries.signature: export declare function lcm(a: number, b: number): number; ; export declare function lcm(a: bigint, b: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Least common multiple, always non-negative. Zero in → zero out.

entries.name: LengthUnit
entries.signature: export type LengthUnit = 'nm' | 'µm' | 'mm' | 'cm' | 'dm' | 'm' | 'km' | 'in' | 'ft' | 'yd' | 'fathom' | 'mi' | 'nmi' | 'au' | 'ly' | 'pc';

entries.name: lerp
entries.signature: export declare function lerp(start: number, end: number, t: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Linear interpolation. `t` outside `[0, 1]` extrapolates. Exact at both ends.

entries.name: limit
entries.signature: export declare function limit(f: RealFunction, x0: number, options?: LimitOptions): ExtrapolationResult;
entries.jsdocSummary: `lim f(x)` as `x → x0`, by Richardson extrapolation of `f(x0 ± h)`. A numerical estimate, not a proof that the limit exists.

entries.name: LimitOptions
entries.signature: export type LimitOptions = ExtrapolationOptions & { /** Approach `x0` from below, above, or both (default). */ readonly side?: LimitSide; };

entries.name: LimitSide
entries.signature: export type LimitSide = 'left' | 'right' | 'both';

entries.name: LinearFit
entries.signature: export type LinearFit = Fit & FitDiagnostics & { readonly slope: number; readonly intercept: number; /** Standard error of the slope: `residualStandardError / sqrt(sum((x - mean x)^2))`. */ readonly slopeStandardError: number | undefined; /** Standard error of the intercept: `residualStandardError * sqrt(1/n + mean(x)^2 / sum((x - mean x)^2))`. */ readonly interceptStandardError: number | undefined; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `y = intercept + slope * x`, with the usual least-squares diagnostics. They use n - 2 residual degrees of freedom (n - k - 1 with k = 1 predictor) and are `undefined` for exactly two points, where no residual freedom is left.

entries.name: linearRegression
entries.signature: export declare function linearRegression(x: Iterable<number>, y: Iterable<number>): LinearFit;
entries.jsdocSummary: Ordinary least-squares line `y = slope * x + intercept`. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` for different lengths, fewer than 2 points, or when x is constant (the slope is undefined).

entries.name: linspace
entries.signature: export declare function linspace(start: number, end: number, count: number): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: `count` evenly spaced numbers from `start` to `end`, both included: `linspace(0, 1, 5)` → `[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]`. `count` 1 gives `[start]`, 0 gives `[]`. The first element is exactly `start` and the last exactly `end`; the span may exceed the float range (`linspace(-1e308, 1e308, 3)` works). Throws `InvalidArgumentError` unless `count` is a non-negative safe integer and `ResourceLimitError` past 10,000,000 elements.

entries.name: ln
entries.signature: export declare function ln(value: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Natural logarithm, correctly rounded to `scale` fraction digits. `ln(1)` is exactly 0; values ≤ 0 throw `InvalidArgumentError`. `ln 2` and `ln 10` are computed once per precision and reused.

entries.name: localeNumberSymbols
entries.signature: export declare function localeNumberSymbols(locale: string): LocaleNumberSymbols;
entries.jsdocSummary: The decimal, group and minus symbols and the digits a locale uses. Cached per locale.

entries.name: LocaleNumberSymbols
entries.signature: export type LocaleNumberSymbols = { decimal: string; group: string; minusSign: string; /** The ten digits `0` to `9` as this locale writes them. */ digits: string[]; };

entries.name: log
entries.signature: export declare function log(value: DecimalInput, base: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Logarithm of `value` in `base` (> 0, ≠ 1), correctly rounded to `scale` fraction digits. Exact results are detected — `log(8, 2)` → `3`, `log(8, 4)` → `1.5` — so `rounding: 'unnecessary'` accepts them.

entries.name: log10
entries.signature: export declare function log10(value: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Base-10 logarithm, correctly rounded: `log10(1000, { scale: 5 })` → `3.00000`.

entries.name: log2
entries.signature: export declare function log2(value: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Base-2 logarithm, correctly rounded: `log2(1024, { scale: 5 })` → `10.00000`.

entries.name: LogarithmicFit
entries.signature: export type LogarithmicFit = Fit & { readonly a: number; readonly b: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `y = a + b * ln(x)`.

entries.name: logarithmicRegression
entries.signature: export declare function logarithmicRegression(x: Iterable<number>, y: Iterable<number>): LogarithmicFit;
entries.jsdocSummary: Logarithmic fit `y = a + b * ln(x)`, by least squares on `ln x`. `r2` is measured on the original y. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` unless every x is positive; `predict` does too.

entries.name: marginOfError
entries.signature: export declare function marginOfError({ stddev: spread, n, level, method }: MarginOfErrorInput): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Half-width of a confidence interval for a mean: critical value times the standard error. `method` is `'t'` by default (needs `n >= 2`), `level` 0.95.

entries.name: MarginOfErrorInput
entries.signature: export type MarginOfErrorInput = { /** Standard deviation of the data (sample, unless you know the population value). */ stddev: number; /** Number of observations. */ n: number; level?: number; method?: IntervalMethod; };

entries.name: MassUnit
entries.signature: export type MassUnit = 'mg' | 'ct' | 'g' | 'kg' | 't' | 'oz' | 'lb' | 'st' | 'ton_us' | 'ton_uk';

entries.name: MATH_ERROR_CODES
entries.signature: export declare const MATH_ERROR_CODES: { /** * A string is not a number in the accepted syntax. * * @fix Pass a plain ASCII decimal string such as `'12.5'` or `'1e3'`, or parse locale text with `@arki/math/parse`. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly numberFormat: 'ARKI_MATH_E001'; /** * An argument is outside what the function accepts. * * @fix Read the message for the argument and fix its value: bounds in order, a positive step, a probability from 0 to 1. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly invalidArgument: 'ARKI_MATH_E002'; /** * Division by zero, or zero raised to a negative power. * * @fix Check the divisor before the call, or choose a result for the zero case in your own code. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly divisionByZero: 'ARKI_MATH_E003'; /** * The exact result needs rounding and no rounding mode was given. * * @fix Pass a scale and a rounding mode, for example `{ scale: 4, rounding: 'halfEven' }`. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly roundingNecessary: 'ARKI_MATH_E004'; /** * A value cannot be represented in the target type. * * @fix Use a `bigint` or `Decimal` input, or keep the value inside the safe integer and finite float range. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly numericRange: 'ARKI_MATH_E005'; /** * A statistic was asked of an empty or too small data set. * * @fix Check the data length first. These limits guard against hostile input. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly resourceLimit: 'ARKI_MATH_E007'; /** * The runtime lacks an `Intl` feature this call depends on. * * @fix Pass `symbols` to parse without `Intl`, or use a runtime with the feature (Hermes on iOS lacks `formatToParts`). * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly unsupportedFeature: 'ARKI_MATH_E008'; /** * A matrix is singular to working precision. * * @fix Check the matrix with `conditionNumber` or `rank`, or use `leastSquares` or `pseudoInverse`. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly singularMatrix: 'ARKI_MATH_E009'; /** * An iterative method did not reach its tolerance. * * @fix Read `.best` for the best estimate, widen the tolerance or iteration limit, or give a better starting bracket. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly convergence: 'ARKI_MATH_E010'; /** * A matrix that must be symmetric positive definite is not. * * @fix Pass a symmetric positive definite matrix, or use LU or QR decomposition instead of Cholesky. * @verify cd packages/math && bun run vitest run src/errors.test.ts */ readonly notPositiveDefinite: 'ARKI_MATH_E011'; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Stable error codes of `@arki/math`.

entries.name: noncentralT
entries.signature: export declare function noncentralT(df: number, ncp: number): ContinuousDistribution;
entries.jsdocSummary: Noncentral t distribution with `df > 0` degrees of freedom and noncentrality `ncp` (|ncp| ≤ 37.62). `cdf` is Lenth's (1989) AS 243 series (~1e-14; a normal approximation is used for df > 4e5); it returns the exact limits 1 / 0 once df/x² underflows. `pdf` uses the Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan power series on the side of 0 where x and ncp share a sign (all terms positive) and close to 0 on the other side; elsewhere it uses the identity f(x) = df/x · [F(x·√(1+2/df); df+2) − F(x; df)], where the cdf difference no longer cancels (accurate to ~1e-15 absolute, so relative accuracy fades only where the density itself is below ~1e-13). `quantile` is the safeguarded Newton solver. With `ncp = 0` it equals `studentT(df)`.

Approximate and possibly fractional; round up yourself for whole months. The result can be passed straight back to `futureValue`.

The default `ddof: 1` is the textbook pooled sample variance `sum((n_i - 1) * s_i^2) / sum(n_i - 1)` (the two-sample t-test's s_p^2, ANOVA's mean square within); `ddof: 0` divides by N. A group of one value adds no spread and, with `ddof: 1`, no degrees of freedom.

entries.signature: export declare function primeFactors(n: number): number[]; ; export declare function primeFactors(n: bigint): bigint[];

entries.name: pythagoreanTriples
entries.signature: export declare function pythagoreanTriples(limit: number, options?: { primitive?: boolean; }): PythagoreanTriple[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Every Pythagorean triple `[a, b, c]` with `a < b < c ≤ limit`, generated by Euclid's formula (a = m² − n², b = 2mn, c = m² + n²), sorted by `c` then `a`. With `primitive: true`, only triples whose sides share no common factor. `limit` must be a non-negative safe integer; the result has roughly `limit · ln(limit) / 2π` entries, so very large limits need a lot of memory.

entries.name: quadraticRoots
entries.signature: export declare function quadraticRoots(a: number, b: number, c: number): QuadraticRoots;
entries.jsdocSummary: Roots of `ax² + bx + c` (`a ≠ 0`). Uses `q = -(b + sign(b)·√D) / 2`, then `q / a` and `c / q`, so neither root suffers cancellation — the small root of `x² - 1e8·x + 1` comes out to full precision. The discriminant is computed with exact products, so near-double roots stay accurate: for Kahan's `94906265.625x² - 189812534x + 94906268.375` it is the exact `7.5625` where the plain float formula gives `0` (a false double root).

entries.signature: export declare function range(end: number): number[]; ; export declare function range(start: number, end: number, step?: number): number[];

Pass the text (or a `Decimal`, whose scale is its written precision): a JS number cannot tell `1.20` from `1.2`. Anything else throws `NumberFormatError`.

entries.signature: export declare function variance(values: Iterable<number>, options?: VarianceOptions): number; ; export declare function variance(values: Iterable<Decimal>, options?: VarianceOptions & Partial<ScaleOptions>): Decimal;

entries.name: log
entries.signature: export declare function log(value: DecimalInput, base: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;

entries.name: log10
entries.signature: export declare function log10(value: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Base-10 logarithm, correctly rounded: `log10(1000, { scale: 5 })` → `3.00000`.

entries.name: log2
entries.signature: export declare function log2(value: DecimalInput, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Base-2 logarithm, correctly rounded: `log2(1024, { scale: 5 })` → `10.00000`.

entries.name: nthRoot
entries.signature: export declare function nthRoot(value: DecimalInput, n: number, options?: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: The n-th root for a positive safe integer `n`. Same exact-or-throw rule as `sqrt` (scale padded up to a multiple of n, then divided by n): `nthRoot('1024', 10)` → `2`. Even roots of negative values throw `InvalidArgumentError`; odd roots keep the sign. Intermediates are capped at 200 000 digits (`ResourceLimitError`), which bounds `n × scale`.

entries.name: PI
entries.signature: export declare function PI(scale: number): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: π to `scale` fraction digits, rounded half-even. Machin's formula, cached per precision.

entries.name: sqrt
entries.signature: export declare function sqrt(value: DecimalInput, options?: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Square root. Without options the result must be exact or it throws `RoundingNecessaryError`: `sqrt(16)` → `4`, `sqrt('2.25')` → `1.5`, `sqrt(2)` throws. The exact result of a value with scale s has scale s/2, after padding an odd s with one zero: `sqrt('1.00')` → `1.0`, `sqrt('0.0001')` → `0.01`, `sqrt('0.4')` (= √0.40) throws.

entries.name: gamma
entries.signature: export declare function gamma(x: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The gamma function Γ(x) for finite `x`. `Γ(n + 1) = n!`, so this is the float factorial for `n > 18`. Positive integers up to 171 are exact products; other values use Lanczos (relative error ~1e-15) with the reflection formula for `x < 0.5`. Poles (`0` and the negative integers) throw `InvalidArgumentError`; a result beyond the double range (`x` above about 171.62, or `x` within ~1e-308 of a pole) throws `NumericRangeError`. Very negative `x` whose true value is below the smallest double returns `0`.

entries.signature: export declare function gammaLn(x: number): number;

entries.signature: export declare const MAX_NONCENTRALITY = 37.62;

With `ncp = 0` it equals `studentT(df)`.

entries.jsdocSummary: Interest earned only: `futureValue − principal`. Exact; with `{ scale }` it is rounded once. `periods` must be a non-negative safe integer.

entries.name: effectiveRate
entries.signature: export declare function effectiveRate(nominalRate: DecimalInput, periodsPerYear: number, options?: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Effective annual rate from a nominal rate compounded `periodsPerYear` times: `(1 + nominal ÷ n)^n − 1`. Computed as an exact fraction and rounded once with `{ scale }`. Without options the exact value is returned when it terminates, and `RoundingNecessaryError` is thrown when it does not.

entries.name: futureValue
entries.signature: export declare function futureValue(principal: DecimalInput, rate: DecimalInput, periods: number, options?: FutureValueOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Balance after `periods`: `principal × (1 + rate)^periods`, plus each `payment` grown to the end (Excel `FV`, negated; see the module doc).

entries.name: FutureValueOptions
entries.signature: export type FutureValueOptions = AnnuityOptions & (ScaleOptions | { scale?: undefined; rounding?: undefined; });
entries.jsdocSummary: `futureValue` options: an optional payment, and `{ scale, rounding }` only together.

entries.signature: export declare function internalRateOfReturn(cashFlows: readonly number[], options?: { guess?: number; tolerance?: number; }): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Internal rate of return as a JS number (the rate that makes NPV zero), like Excel `IRR`. Cash flows start at t = 0 and need at least one negative and one positive value.

entries.name: netPresentValue
entries.signature: export declare function netPresentValue(rate: DecimalInput, cashFlows: readonly DecimalInput[], options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Net present value of `cashFlows` at t = 1..n, like Excel `NPV`: the first flow is discounted one full period. Add a t = 0 flow yourself: `initial.plus(netPresentValue(rate, flows, options))`.

entries.name: nominalRate
entries.signature: export declare function nominalRate(effectiveRate: DecimalInput, periodsPerYear: number, options: ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Nominal annual rate that compounds `periodsPerYear` times to the given effective rate: `n × ((1 + effective)^(1/n) − 1)`.

entries.name: payment
entries.signature: export declare function payment(principal: DecimalInput, rate: DecimalInput, periods: number, options: PaymentOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Excel `PMT`: the level payment that pays off a loan of `principal` over `periods` at `rate` per period.

entries.name: PaymentOptions
entries.signature: export type PaymentOptions = ScaleOptions & { timing?: PaymentTiming; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Options for `payment` and `amortizationSchedule`.

entries.name: PaymentTiming
entries.signature: export type PaymentTiming = 'end' | 'begin';
entries.jsdocSummary: When in the period payments fall: `'end'` is Excel `type` 0, `'begin'` is `type` 1.

entries.name: periodsToReach
entries.signature: export declare function periodsToReach(principal: number, target: number, rate: number, options?: AnnuityOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Periods until the balance goes from `principal` to `target` at `rate` per period: the `periods` that makes `futureValue(principal, rate, periods, options)` equal `target`. Approximate and possibly fractional; round up yourself for whole months. The result can be passed straight back to `futureValue`.

entries.name: presentValue
entries.signature: export declare function presentValue(amount: DecimalInput, rate: DecimalInput, periods: number, options: PresentValueOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Today's worth of `amount` due after `periods`, plus each `payment` discounted to today (Excel `PV`, negated; see the module doc): `(amount + payment × timing × ((1 + rate)^periods − 1) ÷ rate) ÷ (1 + rate)^periods`.

entries.name: PresentValueOptions
entries.signature: export type PresentValueOptions = AnnuityOptions & ScaleOptions;
entries.jsdocSummary: `presentValue` options: an optional payment and the required `{ scale }`.

entries.name: simpleInterest
entries.signature: export declare function simpleInterest(principal: DecimalInput, rate: DecimalInput, periods: DecimalInput): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: `principal × rate × periods`, exact. `periods` may be fractional (pass it as a string or Decimal).

entries.name: AmortizationRow

entries.name: amortizationSchedule
entries.signature: export declare function amortizationSchedule(principal: number, rate: number, periods: number, options?: { timing?: PaymentTiming; }): AmortizationRow[];

entries.name: AnnuityOptions
entries.signature: export type AnnuityOptions = { /** Paid in (positive) or taken out (negative) every period. Defaults to 0. */ payment?: number; /** When in the period the payment falls. Defaults to `'end'`. */ timing?: PaymentTiming; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A level payment made every period, added to the balance (negative to withdraw).

entries.name: compoundInterest
entries.signature: export declare function compoundInterest(principal: number, rate: number, periods: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Interest earned only: `principal × ((1 + rate)^periods − 1)`, via `expm1` so tiny rates do not cancel to 0. `periods` may be fractional or negative.

entries.name: effectiveRate
entries.signature: export declare function effectiveRate(nominalRate: number, periodsPerYear: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Effective annual rate (Excel `EFFECT`) from a nominal rate compounded `periodsPerYear` times: `(1 + nominal ÷ n)^n − 1`. `periodsPerYear` must be positive and may be fractional (0.5 compounds every two years).

entries.name: futureValue
entries.signature: export declare function futureValue(principal: number, rate: number, periods: number, options?: AnnuityOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Balance after `periods`: `principal × (1 + rate)^periods`, plus each `payment` grown to the end (Excel `FV`, negated). `periods` may be fractional or negative (negative discounts).

entries.name: internalRateOfReturn
entries.signature: export declare function internalRateOfReturn(cashFlows: readonly number[], options?: { guess?: number; tolerance?: number; }): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Internal rate of return as a JS number (the rate that makes NPV zero), like Excel `IRR`. Cash flows start at t = 0 and need at least one negative and one positive value.

entries.name: netPresentValue
entries.signature: export declare function netPresentValue(rate: number, cashFlows: readonly number[]): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Net present value of `cashFlows` at t = 1..n, like Excel `NPV`: the first flow is discounted one full period. Add a t = 0 flow yourself: `initial + netPresentValue(rate, flows)`.

entries.name: nominalRate
entries.signature: export declare function nominalRate(effectiveRate: number, periodsPerYear: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Nominal annual rate (Excel `NOMINAL`) that compounds `periodsPerYear` times to the given effective rate: `n × ((1 + effective)^(1/n) − 1)`.

entries.name: payment
entries.signature: export declare function payment(principal: number, rate: number, periods: number, options?: { timing?: PaymentTiming; }): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Excel `PMT`, negated: the level payment that pays off `principal` over `periods` at `rate` per period. `periods` must be positive and may be fractional. A rate of 0 gives `principal ÷ periods`; `timing: 'begin'` divides the payment by `1 + rate`.

entries.name: PaymentTiming
entries.signature: export type PaymentTiming = 'end' | 'begin';
entries.jsdocSummary: When in the period payments fall: `'end'` is Excel `type` 0, `'begin'` is `type` 1.

entries.name: periodsToReach
entries.signature: export declare function periodsToReach(principal: number, target: number, rate: number, options?: AnnuityOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Periods until the balance goes from `principal` to `target` at `rate` per period: the `periods` that makes `futureValue(principal, rate, periods, options)` equal `target`. Approximate and possibly fractional; round up yourself for whole months. The result can be passed straight back to `futureValue`.

entries.name: presentValue
entries.signature: export declare function presentValue(amount: number, rate: number, periods: number, options?: AnnuityOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Today's worth of `amount` due after `periods`, plus each `payment` discounted to today (Excel `PV`, negated): `amount ÷ (1 + rate)^periods + payment × (1 − (1 + rate)^-periods) ÷ rate`. `periods` may be fractional or negative.

entries.name: createFormatter
entries.signature: export declare function createFormatter(defaults: { locale?: string; currency?: string; }): Formatter;
entries.jsdocSummary: Binds a default locale (and optionally a currency) once. The defaults are copied at creation, so later changes to the caller's object have no effect. Per-call `locale` overrides the default; an explicit currency overrides the bound one. Calls without per-call options reuse a pre-resolved `Intl.NumberFormat` and skip cache-key building. `formatCurrency` with no currency anywhere throws `InvalidArgumentError`.

entries.name: CurrencyOptions

entries.name: FileSizeOptions
entries.signature: export type FileSizeOptions = { /** * `'si'` uses powers of 1000 (`kB`), `'iec'` powers of 1024 (`KiB`), `'jedec'` powers of 1024 * with the `KB`/`MB`/`GB` labels most file managers print. Default `'si'`. */ system?: 'si' | 'iec' | 'jedec'; } & FormatOptions;

entries.name: formatCompact
entries.signature: export declare function formatCompact(value: FormatValue, options?: CompactOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Short or long compact form: `formatCompact(1230000)` → `'1.2M'`. Default max 1 fraction digit. With `currency` it is compact money: `formatCompact(1_250_000, { currency: 'USD' })` → `'$1.3M'`.

entries.name: formatCurrency
entries.signature: export declare function formatCurrency(value: FormatValue, currency: string, options?: CurrencyOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats money. Fraction digits come from the currency (2 for USD, 0 for JPY) unless overridden: `formatCurrency(1234.5, 'EUR', { locale: 'de-DE' })` → `'1.234,50 €'`.

entries.name: formatFileSize
entries.signature: export declare function formatFileSize(bytes: number | bigint, options?: FileSizeOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Human file size: `formatFileSize(1536)` → `'1.5 kB'`. Picks the largest unit where the value is at least 1. The number part is locale-aware; the unit label is appended in English (`Intl` has no IEC units). Very large bigints lose precision beyond 2^53, which is invisible at one fraction digit. Rounding can show `'1000 kB'` for 999999 bytes; it does not promote to MB.

entries.name: formatNumber
entries.signature: export declare function formatNumber(value: FormatValue, options?: FormatOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats a number for display: `formatNumber(1234.5)` → `'1,234.5'`. Intl defaults: 0–3 fraction digits.

entries.signature: export type FormatOptions = { /** * BCP 47 locale tag. Default `'en-US'`, so output is the same on every machine * (SSR-safe). Default `'halfUp'`. */ rounding?: Exclude<RoundingMode, 'unnecessary'>; signDisplay?: 'auto' | 'always' | 'exceptZero' | 'negative' | 'never'; };

entries.name: formatPercent
entries.signature: export declare function formatPercent(fraction: FormatValue, options?: FormatOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats a FRACTION as a percent. The input is a fraction, NOT a percentage: `formatPercent(0.125)` → `'12.5%'`, while `formatPercent(12.5)` → `'1,250%'`. Default 0–2 fraction digits.

entries.signature: export type FormatValue = number | bigint | Decimal | string;
entries.jsdocSummary: A formattable value. A string must be a number in plain decimal syntax (`'-1234.50'`).

entries.name: RUNTIME_LOCALE
entries.signature: export declare const RUNTIME_LOCALE = "default";
entries.jsdocSummary: Pass as `locale` to use the runtime's default locale instead of `'en-US'`. It is a word, not `undefined`, so a missing locale can never switch it on by accident.

entries.jsdocSummary: Whether three positive integers are a Pythagorean triple, in any order (the largest is taken as the hypotenuse). Exact: `number` inputs are squared as `bigint`, so large integers are not misjudged by rounding. Non-integers and non-positive values are simply not triples.

entries.name: pythagoreanTriples
entries.signature: export declare function pythagoreanTriples(limit: number, options?: { primitive?: boolean; }): PythagoreanTriple[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Every Pythagorean triple `[a, b, c]` with `a < b < c ≤ limit`, generated by Euclid's formula (a = m² − n², b = 2mn, c = m² + n²), sorted by `c` then `a`. With `primitive: true`, only triples whose sides share no common factor. `limit` must be a non-negative safe integer; the result has roughly `limit · ln(limit) / 2π` entries, so very large limits need a lot of memory.

entries.name: regularPolygon

entries.signature: export declare function signedPolygonArea(vertices: Iterable<Point2>): number;

Do not repeat the first vertex at the end (it is harmless if you do). For a self-intersecting polygon the result is the net of its oppositely wound parts.

entries.name: solveTriangle

entries.name: solveTriangles
entries.signature: export declare function solveTriangles(parts: TriangleParts, options?: TriangleOptions): readonly Triangle[];

Parts that describe no triangle (triangle inequality broken, angles summing to a half turn or more, SSA side too short) give `[]`. entries.name: combinations
entries.signature: export declare function combinations(n: number, k: number): number; ; export declare function combinations(n: bigint, k: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Binomial coefficient C(n, k), the number of ways to choose `k` of `n`. Returns `0` when `k` is outside `0..n`. Uses the multiplicative formula, dividing at every step so values stay integral. The `bigint` form allows at most 100_000 steps and a 100,000-digit result (`ResourceLimitError`).

entries.name: digitSum
entries.signature: export declare function digitSum(n: number | bigint): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Sum of the decimal digits of `|n|`: `digitSum(-123)` is `6`.

entries.name: divisors
entries.signature: export declare function divisors(n: number): number[]; ; export declare function divisors(n: bigint): bigint[];
entries.jsdocSummary: All positive divisors in ascending order: `divisors(28)` is `[1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28]`. Requires `n >= 1`. Built from the prime factorization, so `bigint` input is limited to `n < 2^64`.

entries.name: divmod
entries.signature: export declare function divmod(a: number, b: number): [quotient: number, remainder: number]; ; export declare function divmod(a: bigint, b: bigint): [quotient: bigint, remainder: bigint];
entries.jsdocSummary: Floor division and remainder, like Python's `divmod`: the quotient rounds toward −∞ and the remainder takes the sign of the divisor, so `divmod(-7, 2)` is `[-4, 1]` and `divmod(7, -2)` is `[-4, -1]`.

entries.name: factorial
entries.signature: export declare function factorial(n: number): number; ; export declare function factorial(n: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: `n!`. The `number` form works up to `n = 18`; above that the result is unsafe and it throws `NumericRangeError`. The `bigint` form is capped at `n = 25_205` (results up to 100,000 digits; `ResourceLimitError`).

entries.name: fibonacci
entries.signature: export declare function fibonacci(n: number): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: The n-th Fibonacci number (`F(0) = 0`, `F(1) = 1`) by fast doubling. Always returns a `bigint`. `n` must be a non-negative safe integer at most 100_000 (`ResourceLimitError` above).

entries.name: fromBase
entries.signature: export declare function fromBase(text: string, base: number): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Reads an integer written in `base` 2 to 36 into a `bigint`: `fromBase('ff', 16)` is `255n`. An optional leading `-` or `+` is allowed and digits are case insensitive. Anything else (spaces, `_`, a `0x` prefix, a digit too large for the base, empty text) throws `NumberFormatError`.

entries.name: gcd
entries.signature: export declare function gcd(a: number, b: number): number; ; export declare function gcd(a: bigint, b: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Greatest common divisor, always non-negative. `gcd(0, 0)` is `0`.

entries.name: isEven
entries.signature: export declare function isEven(n: number | bigint): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: True when `n` is divisible by 2. Zero is even.

entries.name: isOdd
entries.signature: export declare function isOdd(n: number | bigint): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: True when `n` is not divisible by 2. Negative odd numbers are odd.

entries.name: isPrime
entries.signature: export declare function isPrime(n: number): boolean; ; export declare function isPrime(n: bigint): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: Exact primality test by Miller–Rabin with a fixed base set that is deterministic for every `n < 2^64`. Values below 2 are not prime. At or above 2^64 it throws `NumericRangeError` rather than guess.

entries.name: lcm
entries.signature: export declare function lcm(a: number, b: number): number; ; export declare function lcm(a: bigint, b: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Least common multiple, always non-negative. Zero in → zero out.

entries.name: modInverse
entries.signature: export declare function modInverse(a: bigint, modulus: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Modular inverse of `a` mod `modulus` in `[0, modulus)`, by extended Euclid. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` when `gcd(a, modulus) !== 1`.

entries.name: modPow
entries.signature: export declare function modPow(base: bigint, exponent: bigint, modulus: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: `base ** exponent mod modulus`, in `[0, modulus)`. Requires `exponent >= 0` and `modulus > 0`. Square-and-multiply.

entries.name: permutations
entries.signature: export declare function permutations(n: number, k: number): number; ; export declare function permutations(n: bigint, k: bigint): bigint;
entries.jsdocSummary: Ordered selections P(n, k) = n! / (n − k)!. Returns `0` when `k` is outside `0..n`. The `bigint` form allows at most 100_000 terms and a 100,000-digit result.

entries.name: primeFactors
entries.signature: export declare function primeFactors(n: number): number[]; ; export declare function primeFactors(n: bigint): bigint[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Prime factors in ascending order, with multiplicity: `360` gives `[2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5]`. Values below 2 give `[]`; negatives throw `InvalidArgumentError`. Trial division by 2, 3 and `6k ± 1` up to 1e6, then Pollard's rho (Brent) with Miller–Rabin. Throws `NumericRangeError` for `n >= 2^64`.

entries.name: toBase
entries.signature: export declare function toBase(value: number | bigint, base: number): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Writes an integer in `base` 2 to 36 with lowercase digits: `toBase(255, 16)` is `'ff'`, `toBase(-10, 2)` is `'-1010'`. A `number` must be a safe integer; a `bigint` is exact at any size. No prefix (`0x`) is added.

entries.name: integrate
entries.signature: export declare function integrate(f: RealFunction, bounds: readonly [number, number], options?: IntegrateOptions): IntegrationResult;
entries.jsdocSummary: `∫ f(x) dx` from `bounds[0]` to `bounds[1]`, with an error estimate. Either bound may be infinite. See the module docs for the methods, the tolerance and the failure policy.

entries.name: IntegrateOptions
entries.signature: export type IntegrateOptions = { /** `'gaussKronrod'` (default, adaptive G7–K15) or `'tanhSinh'` (double-exponential, for endpoint singularities). */ readonly method?: IntegrationMethod; /** Absolute tolerance on the error estimate (default `1e-12`). */ readonly absoluteTolerance?: number; /** Relative tolerance, times `|value|` (default `1e-10`). */ readonly relativeTolerance?: number; /** Most calls of `f` before `IntegrationConvergenceError` (default 20,000). */ readonly maxEvaluations?: number; };

entries.name: IntegrationConvergenceError
entries.signature: export declare class IntegrationConvergenceError extends ConvergenceError { /** The best value, its error estimate and the evaluations spent (sign already applied for reversed bounds). */ readonly best: IntegrationResult; constructor(message: string, best: IntegrationResult); }
entries.jsdocSummary: `integrate` missed its tolerance; `best` is the best estimate it reached.

entries.name: IntegrationMethod
entries.signature: export type IntegrationMethod = 'gaussKronrod' | 'tanhSinh';

entries.name: IntegrationResult
entries.signature: export type IntegrationResult = { readonly value: number; /** Estimated absolute error of `value`. */ readonly errorEstimate: number; /** Calls of `f`. */ readonly evaluations: number; };

entries.name: RealFunction
entries.signature: export type RealFunction = (x: number) => number;
entries.jsdocSummary: A real function of one real variable, evaluated on float64.

entries.name: angleBetween
entries.signature: export declare function angleBetween(a: Vector, b: Vector): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The angle between two vectors in radians, in `[0, π]`. Uses Kahan's `2·atan2(‖û − v̂‖, ‖û + v̂‖)` on the unit vectors, which stays accurate for nearly parallel and nearly opposite vectors where `acos(cos θ)` loses half its digits. Throws `DivisionByZeroError` if either vector is zero.

entries.name: choleskyDecompose
entries.signature: export declare function choleskyDecompose(a: Matrix, options?: SymmetryOptions): CholeskyDecomposition;
entries.jsdocSummary: `A = L·Lᵀ` for a symmetric positive definite matrix (LAPACK `dpotrf`): about half the work of LU, and no pivoting is needed. Symmetry is checked like `symmetricEigenvalues` (`InvalidArgumentError` beyond the tolerance; the factorization uses `(A + Aᵀ) / 2`). Throws `NotPositiveDefiniteError` when a diagonal pivot is `≤ 0`, the LAPACK rule, which makes this the standard positive-definiteness test. A singular positive semidefinite matrix may pass with a tiny diagonal entry or throw, depending on rounding.

entries.name: CholeskyDecomposition
entries.signature: export type CholeskyDecomposition = { /** Lower-triangular `L` with a positive diagonal. */ lower: number[][]; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `A = L·Lᵀ`, from `choleskyDecompose`.

entries.name: choleskySolve
entries.signature: export declare function choleskySolve(a: Matrix, b: Vector, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[]; ; export declare function choleskySolve(a: Matrix, b: Matrix, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: Solves `A·x = b` for a symmetric positive definite `A` by Cholesky: about twice as fast as `solve`, and as accurate. `b` is a vector or a matrix of right-hand-side columns, as for `solve`. Symmetry is checked with the default tolerance (see `choleskyDecompose`). A pivot `d` with `|d| ≤ n · Number.EPSILON · ‖A‖∞` (or `{ tolerance }`, absolute; the same quantity `solve` tests, since for this matrix `d` equals LU's pivot) throws `SingularMatrixError`; a pivot below `−tolerance` throws `NotPositiveDefiniteError`.

entries.name: conditionNumber
entries.signature: export declare function conditionNumber(a: Matrix): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The 2-norm condition number `σ₁ / σₖ` (largest over smallest singular value) of any `m×n` matrix: about how many times a relative error in `A` or `b` can be magnified in the solution of `A·x = b` or a least-squares fit. `1` for an orthogonal matrix; `Infinity` (as NumPy's `cond` returns) when the smallest singular value is exactly `0`, the one case in this module that returns a non-finite number, since the condition number of a singular matrix is infinite by definition.

entries.name: cross
entries.signature: export declare function cross(a: Vector, b: Vector): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Cross product of two 3-vectors; perpendicular to both, right-handed.

entries.name: determinant
entries.signature: export declare function determinant(a: Matrix): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The determinant, as `sign(P) · Π u_kk` from an LU factorization: O(n³), where cofactor expansion is O(n!). A singular matrix gives `0` or a value tiny next to the entries; it never throws for that. Throws `NumericRangeError` if the product overflows.

entries.name: dot
entries.signature: export declare function dot(a: Vector, b: Vector): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Dot product `Σ aᵢ·bᵢ`. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` for different lengths.

entries.name: eigenDecompose
entries.signature: export declare function eigenDecompose(a: Matrix): EigenDecomposition;
entries.jsdocSummary: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of any real square matrix: `A·v = λ·v` for `λ = values[k]`, `v = vectors[k]`. Values are sorted as in `eigenvalues`. Each vector has unit length with its largest-magnitude entry real and positive; a real eigenvalue's vector has real entries, and conjugate eigenvalues have conjugate vectors. For a defective matrix the vectors of a repeated eigenvalue are (nearly) parallel: there is no full basis to find. Throws `ConvergenceError` if the QR iteration stalls.

entries.name: EigenDecomposition
entries.signature: export type EigenDecomposition = { /** The eigenvalues, sorted by real part, then imaginary part; a real one has `im === 0`. */ values: Complex[]; /** `vectors[k]` is a unit eigenvector for `values[k]` (real entries for a real eigenvalue). */ vectors: Complex[][]; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Eigenpairs of a general real matrix, from `eigenDecompose`.

entries.name: eigenvalues
entries.signature: export declare function eigenvalues(a: Matrix): Complex[];
entries.jsdocSummary: The eigenvalues of any real square matrix, as `Complex` values sorted by real part, then imaginary part, repeated by multiplicity. A real eigenvalue has an imaginary part of exactly `0`; complex ones come in conjugate pairs. For a symmetric matrix, `symmetricEigenvalues` is faster and returns plain numbers. Throws `ConvergenceError` if the QR iteration stalls.

entries.name: identity
entries.signature: export declare function identity(n: number): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: The `n × n` identity matrix. Throws `ResourceLimitError` past 10,000,000 elements.

entries.name: inverse
entries.signature: export declare function inverse(a: Matrix, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: The inverse `A⁻¹`, so that `A·A⁻¹ = I`. Throws `SingularMatrixError` when `A` is singular to working precision. To solve `A·x = b`, call `solve`: it is faster and more accurate than `multiply(inverse(A), b)`.

entries.name: leastSquares
entries.signature: export declare function leastSquares(a: Matrix, b: Vector, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[]; ; export declare function leastSquares(a: Matrix, b: Matrix, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: The least-squares solution of `A·x ≈ b` for any `m×n` matrix: the `x` that minimizes `‖A·x − b‖₂`. `b` is a vector (gives `x`, length `n`) or a matrix of right-hand-side columns (gives an `n`-row matrix of solution columns).

entries.name: luDecompose
entries.signature: export declare function luDecompose(a: Matrix): LuDecomposition;
entries.jsdocSummary: `P·A = L·U` for a square matrix, with partial pivoting (the largest remaining entry in each column becomes the pivot, so every multiplier in `L` has magnitude at most 1). Never throws for a singular matrix: `upper` then has a zero, or tiny, diagonal entry.

entries.name: LuDecomposition
entries.signature: export type LuDecomposition = { /** Unit lower-triangular factor `L` (ones on the diagonal). */ lower: number[][]; /** Upper-triangular factor `U`; a zero (or tiny) diagonal entry means `A` is singular. */ upper: number[][]; /** Row `i` of `P·A` is row `permutation[i]` of `A`. */ permutation: number[]; /** Sign of the permutation: `1` for an even number of row swaps, `-1` for odd. */ sign: 1 | -1; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `P·A = L·U`, from `luDecompose`.

entries.name: matrix
entries.signature: export declare function matrix(rows: Matrix): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: A validated copy of `rows`: throws unless it is a non-empty, rectangular array of non-empty rows of finite numbers. Use it at a trust boundary (parsed JSON, user input); every other function validates on its own.

entries.name: Matrix
entries.signature: export type Matrix = readonly Vector[];
entries.jsdocSummary: A matrix: a non-empty array of equally long, non-empty rows of finite numbers.

entries.name: minus
entries.signature: export declare function minus(a: Vector, b: Vector): number[]; ; export declare function minus(a: Matrix, b: Matrix): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: Element-wise difference `a − b` of two vectors, or of two matrices of the same shape.

entries.name: multiply
entries.signature: export declare function multiply(a: Matrix, b: Matrix): number[][]; ; export declare function multiply(a: Matrix, b: Vector): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: The matrix product `A·B` (`m×n` times `n×p` gives `m×p`), or the matrix-vector product `A·v` (an `m`-vector). For a row vector times a matrix, use `multiply(transpose(A), v)`. For scaling by a number, see `times`.

entries.name: norm
entries.signature: export declare function norm(v: Vector, p?: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The p-norm `(Σ |vᵢ|^p)^(1/p)`: Euclidean length by default, `1` for the taxicab sum, `Infinity` for the largest magnitude. `p` must be at least 1 (below 1 it is not a norm). Scaled by the largest magnitude first, so `norm([3e200, 4e200])` is `5e200` instead of overflowing.

entries.name: normalize
entries.signature: export declare function normalize(v: Vector): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: The unit vector in the direction of `v`. Throws `DivisionByZeroError` for the zero vector.

entries.name: plus
entries.signature: export declare function plus(a: Vector, b: Vector): number[]; ; export declare function plus(a: Matrix, b: Matrix): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: Element-wise sum of two vectors, or of two matrices of the same shape.

entries.name: projection
entries.signature: export declare function projection(v: Vector, onto: Vector): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: The vector projection of `v` onto `onto`: `(v·onto / onto·onto)·onto`. Throws `DivisionByZeroError` when `onto` is the zero vector.

entries.name: pseudoInverse
entries.signature: export declare function pseudoInverse(a: Matrix, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: The Moore–Penrose pseudo-inverse `A⁺` (`n×m` for an `m×n` matrix) from the SVD: `V·Σ⁺·Uᵀ`, where `Σ⁺` inverts the singular values above `max(m, n) · Number.EPSILON · σ₁` (NumPy's `pinv` default) and zeroes the rest; `{ tolerance }` sets an absolute cut-off instead. `A⁺·b` is the minimum-norm least-squares solution, but `leastSquares` computes that faster and more accurately.

entries.name: qrDecompose
entries.signature: export declare function qrDecompose(a: Matrix, options?: QrOptions): QrDecomposition;
entries.jsdocSummary: `A·P = Q·R` for any `m×n` matrix, by Householder reflections (LAPACK `dgeqp3`, or `dgeqrf` with `{ pivoting: false }`). `Q` is the thin `m×k` factor with `k = min(m, n)`; `R` is `k×n`. Each diagonal entry of `R` is made non-negative (flipping the matching column of `Q`), so without pivoting the factorization of a full-rank `A` is unique. `rank` counts the `|r_kk|` above `max(m, n) · Number.EPSILON · |r₀₀|`, or above `{ tolerance }` (absolute). Backward stable: `‖A·P − Q·R‖ ≈ n · ε · ‖A‖`. Never throws for a rank-deficient matrix.

entries.name: QrDecomposition
entries.signature: export type QrDecomposition = { /** `Q`, `m×k` with orthonormal columns. */ orthogonal: number[][]; /** `R`, `k×n` upper triangular (trapezoidal when `n > m`), with a non-negative diagonal. */ upper: number[][]; /** Column `j` of `A·P` is column `permutation[j]` of `A`. */ permutation: number[]; /** The number of diagonal entries of `R` above the tolerance: the numerical rank, with pivoting. */ rank: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `A·P = Q·R`, from `qrDecompose`; `k = min(m, n)` for an `m×n` matrix `A`.

entries.name: QrOptions
entries.signature: export type QrOptions = ToleranceOptions & { /** * Column pivoting (default `true`): each step takes the remaining column of * largest norm, so `|r_kk|` falls along the diagonal and `rank` is reliable. * `false` gives plain Householder QR of `A` itself (`permutation` is then the * identity). */ pivoting?: boolean; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Options for `qrDecompose`.

entries.name: rank
entries.signature: export declare function rank(a: Matrix, options?: RankOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The number of linearly independent rows (equivalently, columns) of any `m×n` matrix. By default it counts the singular values above `max(m, n) · Number.EPSILON · σ₁` (σ₁ the largest), the rule of NumPy's `matrix_rank`, so `rank`, `pseudoInverse` and `leastSquares` agree. `{ method: 'elimination' }` counts row echelon pivots above `max(m, n) · Number.EPSILON · ‖A‖∞` instead. `{ tolerance }` replaces the default with an absolute threshold for whichever quantity is counted.

entries.name: RankOptions
entries.signature: export type RankOptions = ToleranceOptions & { /** * `'svd'` (the default) counts singular values above the tolerance, the * reliable rank test. `'elimination'` counts pivots of row echelon form with * partial pivoting: several times faster, but on badly conditioned input it * can miss a near-dependence that the singular values show. */ method?: 'svd' | 'elimination'; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Options for `rank`.

entries.name: singularValueDecompose
entries.signature: export declare function singularValueDecompose(a: Matrix): SingularValueDecomposition;
entries.jsdocSummary: `A = U·Σ·Vᵀ` for any `m×n` matrix, in thin form: `values` holds the `k = min(m, n)` singular values, descending; `left[k]` and `right[k]` are the matching unit singular vectors, so `transpose(left)` is the `m×k` factor `U` and `right` is `Vᵀ` (NumPy's `Vh`). Each pair's sign is fixed so that the largest-magnitude entry of `left[k]` (the first, on a tie) is positive. Throws like `singularValues`.

entries.name: SingularValueDecomposition
entries.signature: export type SingularValueDecomposition = { /** The `min(m, n)` singular values, descending, all `≥ 0`. */ values: number[]; /** `left[k]` is the unit left singular vector (length `m`) for `values[k]`; together they are orthonormal. */ left: number[][]; /** `right[k]` is the unit right singular vector (length `n`) for `values[k]`; together they are orthonormal. */ right: number[][]; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `A = Σₖ values[k] · left[k] · right[k]ᵀ`, from `singularValueDecompose`.

entries.name: singularValues
entries.signature: export declare function singularValues(a: Matrix): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: The singular values of any `m×n` matrix: `min(m, n)` of them, descending, all `≥ 0` (the square roots of the eigenvalues of `AᵀA`, computed without forming it). Golub–Kahan–Reinsch: backward stable, so each value is within about `max(m, n) · ε · σ₁` of the exact one. Throws `ConvergenceError` if the QR iteration stalls (see the module docs). Faster than `singularValueDecompose`: no singular vectors are accumulated.

entries.name: solve
entries.signature: export declare function solve(a: Matrix, b: Vector, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[]; ; export declare function solve(a: Matrix, b: Matrix, options?: ToleranceOptions): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: Solves `A·x = b` for a square `A`, by LU with partial pivoting. `b` is a vector (gives `x`) or a matrix of right-hand-side columns (gives a matrix of solution columns). Throws `SingularMatrixError` when `A` is singular to working precision; see the module docs for the tolerance.

entries.name: symmetricEigenDecompose
entries.signature: export declare function symmetricEigenDecompose(a: Matrix, options?: SymmetryOptions): SymmetricEigenDecomposition;
entries.jsdocSummary: Eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix, so that `A = V·Λ·Vᵀ` with `V = transpose(vectors)`. Values ascend; `vectors[k]` belongs to `values[k]`, has unit length, and its largest-magnitude entry is positive. Throws like `symmetricEigenvalues`.

entries.name: SymmetricEigenDecomposition
entries.signature: export type SymmetricEigenDecomposition = { /** The eigenvalues, ascending, repeated by multiplicity. */ values: number[]; /** `vectors[k]` is the unit eigenvector for `values[k]`; together they are orthonormal. */ vectors: number[][]; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `A = V·Λ·Vᵀ`, from `symmetricEigenDecompose`.

entries.name: symmetricEigenvalues
entries.signature: export declare function symmetricEigenvalues(a: Matrix, options?: SymmetryOptions): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: The eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix, ascending, repeated by multiplicity. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` when `A` is not symmetric within the tolerance (see the module docs, or pass `{ tolerance }`), and `ConvergenceError` if the QL iteration stalls. Faster than `symmetricEigenDecompose`: no eigenvectors are accumulated.

entries.name: SymmetryOptions
entries.signature: export type SymmetryOptions = { /** * Largest accepted `|a[i][j] − a[j][i]|`, absolute. Defaults to * `n · Number.EPSILON · ‖A‖∞`, which accepts the rounding noise of a * matrix computed in floating point; `0` demands exact symmetry. */ tolerance?: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Options for the symmetric eigen solvers.

entries.name: times
entries.signature: export declare function times(a: Vector, k: number): number[]; ; export declare function times(a: Matrix, k: number): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: Every element multiplied by the scalar `k`. For the matrix product, see `multiply`.

entries.name: ToleranceOptions
entries.signature: export type ToleranceOptions = { /** * Absolute pivot threshold. A pivot whose magnitude is at or below it * counts as zero. Defaults to the size-and-norm-relative rule in the module * docs; `0` treats only exact zeros as zero. */ tolerance?: number; };

entries.name: trace
entries.signature: export declare function trace(a: Matrix): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Sum of the diagonal of a square matrix.

entries.name: transpose
entries.signature: export declare function transpose(a: Matrix): number[][];
entries.jsdocSummary: Rows become columns: `transpose(A)[j][i] === A[i][j]`.

entries.name: Vector
entries.signature: export type Vector = readonly number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: A vector: a non-empty array of finite numbers.

entries.name: approxEqual
entries.signature: export declare function approxEqual(a: number, b: number, tolerance?: number): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: Tolerant equality for floats. `tolerance` is relative to the larger magnitude (and absolute near zero), so it works for both `0.1 + 0.2 ≈ 0.3` and `1e12 + 0.001 ≈ 1e12`.

entries.name: Bounds
entries.signature: export type Bounds = '[]' | '[)' | '(]' | '()';
entries.jsdocSummary: Interval notation: `[` / `]` include the bound, `(` / `)` exclude it.

entries.name: clamp
entries.signature: export declare function clamp(x: number, min: number, max: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Limits `x` to `[min, max]`, both ends included.

entries.name: inRange
entries.signature: export declare function inRange(x: number, min: number, max: number, bounds?: Bounds): boolean;
entries.jsdocSummary: Is `x` inside the interval? Defaults to `[min, max)`, the usual half-open range.

entries.name: inverseLerp
entries.signature: export declare function inverseLerp(start: number, end: number, x: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The `t` for which `lerp(start, end, t) === x`.

entries.name: lerp
entries.signature: export declare function lerp(start: number, end: number, t: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Linear interpolation. `t` outside `[0, 1]` extrapolates. Exact at both ends.

entries.name: linspace
entries.signature: export declare function linspace(start: number, end: number, count: number): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: `count` evenly spaced numbers from `start` to `end`, both included: `linspace(0, 1, 5)` → `[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]`. `count` 1 gives `[start]`, 0 gives `[]`. The first element is exactly `start` and the last exactly `end`; the span may exceed the float range (`linspace(-1e308, 1e308, 3)` works). Throws `InvalidArgumentError` unless `count` is a non-negative safe integer and `ResourceLimitError` past 10,000,000 elements.

entries.name: range
entries.signature: export declare function range(end: number): number[]; ; export declare function range(start: number, end: number, step?: number): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Numbers from `start` up to but excluding `end`, `step` apart (default 1): `range(5)` → `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`, `range(0, 1, 0.25)` → `[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75]`. A negative `step` counts down (`range(3, 0, -1)` → `[3, 2, 1]`). Each element is `start + i * step`, so fractional steps do not drift. A step pointing away from `end` gives `[]`. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` for a zero or non-finite step and `ResourceLimitError` past 10,000,000 elements.

entries.name: remap
entries.signature: export declare function remap(x: number, inStart: number, inEnd: number, outStart: number, outEnd: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Maps `x` from one range onto another: `remap(5, 0, 10, 0, 100)` → `50`.

entries.name: round
entries.signature: export declare function round(x: number, places?: number, mode?: RoundingMode): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Rounds the number you typed, not its binary approximation: `round(1.005, 2)` is `1.01` (plain `Math.round(1.005 * 100) / 100` gives `1`). Negative `places` round to tens, hundreds, ...

entries.name: roundTo
entries.signature: export declare function roundTo(x: number, step: number, mode?: RoundingMode): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Rounds to the nearest multiple of `step`, measured from zero: `roundTo(127.3, 5)` → `125`.

entries.name: roundToSignificant
entries.signature: export declare function roundToSignificant(x: number, digits: number, mode?: RoundingMode): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Rounds to `digits` significant figures, on the number you typed: `roundToSignificant(123_456, 2)` is `120000`, `roundToSignificant(0.012_345, 3)` is `0.0123`. A number with fewer digits is returned as is (nothing is padded). Works for every finite double, from subnormals to `6.02214076e23` and beyond: the digits are those of the number's shortest decimal text, `String(x)`. Throws `NumericRangeError` only when rounding up past the largest double (`roundToSignificant(1.7976931348623157e308, 1)` would be `2e308`).

entries.name: significantDigits
entries.signature: export declare function significantDigits(value: string | Decimal): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Counts the significant figures in a written number by the textbook rules: leading zeros never count, zeros between digits always count, and trailing zeros count only when there is a decimal point. `'1200'` → 2, `'1200.'` → 4, `'0.00120'` → 3, `'1.20e3'` → 3. The exponent is ignored. Zero counts its written zeros after the point (`'0'` → 1, `'0.00'` → 2). Pass the text (or a `Decimal`, whose scale is its written precision): a JS number cannot tell `1.20` from `1.2`. Anything else throws `NumberFormatError`.

entries.name: localeNumberSymbols
entries.signature: export declare function localeNumberSymbols(locale: string): LocaleNumberSymbols;
entries.jsdocSummary: The decimal, group and minus symbols and the digits a locale uses. Cached per locale.

entries.name: LocaleNumberSymbols
entries.signature: export type LocaleNumberSymbols = { decimal: string; group: string; minusSign: string; /** The ten digits `0` to `9` as this locale writes them. */ digits: string[]; };

entries.name: parseDecimal
entries.signature: export declare function parseDecimal(input: string, options?: ParseOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Like `parseNumber` (lenient, locale-aware) but exact: every digit survives in the returned `Decimal`.

entries.name: parseNumber
entries.signature: export declare function parseNumber(input: string, options?: ParseOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Parses a locale-formatted number: `parseNumber('1.234,56', { locale: 'de-DE' })` → `1234.56`. Lenient and locale-aware; for strict ASCII input use `decimal()`.

entries.name: ParseOptions
entries.signature: export type ParseOptions = { /** BCP 47 locale tag. Default `'en-US'`. Ignored when `symbols` is given. */ locale?: string; /** * The separators to read, instead of asking `Intl` for the locale's: * `{ decimal: ',', group: '.' }`. Minus defaults to `'-'`, digits to ASCII. */ symbols?: ParseSymbols; };

entries.name: ParseSymbols
entries.signature: export type ParseSymbols = { decimal: string; group: string; minusSign?: string; /** The ten digits `0` to `9`. Default ASCII. */ digits?: readonly string[]; };

entries.name: addPolynomials

Uses `q = -(b + sign(b)·√D) / 2`, then `q / a` and `c / q`, so neither root suffers cancellation — the small root of `x² - 1e8·x + 1` comes out to full precision.
