entries.name: bisect
entries.signature: export declare function bisect(f: RealFunction, bracket: readonly [number, number], options?: RootOptions): RootResult;
entries.jsdocSummary: The root of a continuous `f` inside `bracket`, by bisection. Each step halves the bracket, so reaching a tolerance `t` from width `w` takes `ceil(log2(w / t))` steps; `errorEstimate` bounds the distance to a sign change.

entries.name: findRoot
entries.signature: export declare function findRoot(f: RealFunction, bracket: readonly [number, number], options?: RootOptions): RootResult;
entries.jsdocSummary: The root of a continuous `f` inside `bracket`, by Brent's method. `f(a)` and `f(b)` must have opposite signs (or one of them be 0). `errorEstimate` is the width of the final bracket, so `root` is within it of a sign change.

entries.name: findRoots
entries.signature: export declare function findRoots(f: RealFunction, interval: readonly [number, number], options?: FindRootsOptions): RootResult[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Every root that a sign-change scan of `interval` can see, ascending. `f` is evaluated on `samples + 1` evenly spaced points (default `samples` 100); grid points where `f` is exactly 0 are reported as they are, and each sub-interval whose ends differ in sign is refined by Brent's method. A grid point where `f` has no finite value (it returns `NaN` or `±Infinity`, or throws a `MathError`, as `sqrt(x)` does for `x < 0`) is a gap: no sub-interval that touches it is refined, and the scan goes on. The `iterations`/`evaluations` of each result count only its refinement; the scan itself costs `samples + 1` evaluations.

entries.name: FindRootsOptions
entries.signature: export type FindRootsOptions = RootOptions & { /** Number of equal sub-intervals scanned for a sign change (default 100). */ readonly samples?: number; };

entries.name: newton
entries.signature: export declare function newton(f: RealFunction, df: RealFunction, x0: number, options?: NewtonOptions): RootResult;
entries.jsdocSummary: A root of `f` near `x0` by Newton's method, given the derivative `df`. Unbracketed steps are damped (halved until `|f|` decreases); with `{ bracket }` the method falls back to bisection whenever Newton would leave the bracket or stall, and `errorEstimate` is at most the bracket width.

entries.name: NewtonOptions
entries.signature: export type NewtonOptions = RootOptions & { /** A sign-change bracket containing `x0`; turns on the bisection fallback of `rtsafe`. */ readonly bracket?: readonly [number, number]; };

entries.name: RealFunction

entries.jsdocSummary: A real function of one real variable, evaluated on float64.

entries.name: confidenceInterval
entries.signature: export declare function confidenceInterval(values: Iterable<number>, options?: ConfidenceIntervalOptions): ConfidenceInterval;
entries.jsdocSummary: Confidence interval for the mean of `values`, from the exact critical value of the normal (`'z'`) or Student t with `n - 1` degrees of freedom (`'t'`, the default). The spread is the sample standard deviation (`ddof` 1) unless you pass `ddof: 0`. Needs at least 2 values.

entries.name: ConfidenceInterval

entries.name: ExponentialFit

entries.name: exponentialRegression
entries.signature: export declare function exponentialRegression(x: Iterable<number>, y: Iterable<number>): ExponentialFit;

entries.jsdocSummary: Confidence-interval method: `'z'` (normal critical value) or `'t'` (Student's t, for estimated spread).

entries.name: LogarithmicFit

entries.jsdocSummary: `y = a + b * ln(x)`.

entries.name: logarithmicRegression
entries.signature: export declare function logarithmicRegression(x: Iterable<number>, y: Iterable<number>): LogarithmicFit;
entries.jsdocSummary: Logarithmic fit `y = a + b * ln(x)`, by least squares on `ln x`. `r2` is measured on the original y. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` unless every x is positive; `predict` does too.

entries.signature: export declare function mean(values: Iterable<number>): number; ; export declare function mean(values: Iterable<Decimal>, options?: ScaleOptions): Decimal;

Like `Decimal.dividedBy`, it throws `RoundingNecessaryError` when the result does not terminate (`[1, 1, 2]`) unless you pass `{ scale, rounding }`.

entries.name: MeanSampleSizeInput
entries.signature: export type MeanSampleSizeInput = { marginOfError: number; stddev: number; level?: number; proportion?: never; };

entries.signature: export declare function median(values: Iterable<number>): number; ; export declare function median(values: Iterable<Decimal>): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Middle value; for an even count, the average of the two middle values. Throws `EmptyDataError` when empty. Exact median of `Decimal` values; the midpoint of two middles, `(a + b) / 2`, is always exact in decimal.

entries.name: minMax
entries.signature: export declare function minMax(values: Iterable<number>): MinMax; ; export declare function minMax(values: Iterable<Decimal>): { min: Decimal; max: Decimal; };

entries.name: MinMax
entries.signature: export type MinMax = { min: number; max: number; };

entries.name: mode
entries.signature: export declare function mode(values: Iterable<number>): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Every most-frequent value, ascending. Ties return all tied values; an empty input gives `[]`.

entries.name: percentile
entries.signature: export declare function percentile(values: Iterable<number>, p: number, options?: QuantileOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The `p`-th percentile, `p` in `[0, 100]`. By default linear interpolation between closest ranks (R-7: Excel `PERCENTILE.INC`, NumPy default); pass `{ method }` for any other Hyndman–Fan definition (see `QUANTILE_METHODS`). Equal to `quantile(values, p / 100, options)`. Throws `EmptyDataError` when empty and `InvalidArgumentError` when `p` is out of range.

entries.name: percentileRank
entries.signature: export declare function percentileRank(values: Iterable<number>, score: number, options?: PercentileRankOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Where `score` falls in `values`, as a percentage in `[0, 100]` — the inverse of `percentile`. `kind` says how values equal to the score count (see `PercentileRankKind`); the default `'mean'` counts half of them, so the median of distinct values ranks 50. `score` need not be one of the values. Matches SciPy's `percentileofscore(values, score, kind)`. Throws `EmptyDataError` when empty.

entries.name: PercentileRankKind
entries.signature: export type PercentileRankKind = 'strict' | 'weak' | 'mean' | 'rank';
entries.jsdocSummary: How `percentileRank` counts values equal to the score (the `kind` of SciPy's `percentileofscore`); with B values below and E equal, out of N: - `'strict'`: B / N, the share strictly below. - `'weak'`: (B + E) / N, the share at or below (the empirical CDF). - `'mean'` (default): (B + E / 2) / N, the textbook percentile rank: half of the ties count as below. - `'rank'`: SciPy's default, the average of the ranks the ties would take: (B + (E + 1) / 2) / N when E > 0, else B / N.

entries.name: PercentileRankOptions
entries.signature: export type PercentileRankOptions = { kind?: PercentileRankKind; };

entries.name: PolynomialFit
entries.signature: export type PolynomialFit = Fit & FitDiagnostics & { readonly coefficients: readonly number[]; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `y = c[0] + c[1] * x + c[2] * x^2 + ...`, lowest degree first. Diagnostics use k = degree predictors, so n - degree - 1 residual degrees of freedom.

entries.name: polynomialRegression
entries.signature: export declare function polynomialRegression(x: Iterable<number>, y: Iterable<number>, degree: number): PolynomialFit;
entries.jsdocSummary: Least-squares polynomial of the given `degree`, by Householder QR with column pivoting on the Vandermonde matrix (never the normal equations, which square its condition number; NumPy's `polyfit` uses an SVD to the same end). Coefficients are lowest degree first (`[c0, c1, ...]`); `r2` is measured on the original y.

entries.name: pooledStddev
entries.signature: export declare function pooledStddev(samples: Iterable<Iterable<number> | SampleSummary>, options?: VarianceOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Square root of `pooledVariance`, with the same groups and `ddof` convention (sample by default).

entries.name: pooledVariance
entries.signature: export declare function pooledVariance(samples: Iterable<Iterable<number> | SampleSummary>, options?: VarianceOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Pooled variance of two or more groups that share one spread: the within-group sums of squared deviations, added, over the pooled degrees of freedom, `sum(SS_i) / (N - g * ddof)` for g groups of N values in all. The default `ddof: 1` is the textbook pooled sample variance `sum((n_i - 1) * s_i^2) / sum(n_i - 1)` (the two-sample t-test's s_p^2, ANOVA's mean square within); `ddof: 0` divides by N. A group of one value adds no spread and, with `ddof: 1`, no degrees of freedom.

entries.name: PowerFit
entries.signature: export type PowerFit = Fit & { readonly a: number; readonly b: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `y = a * x^b`.

entries.name: powerRegression
entries.signature: export declare function powerRegression(x: Iterable<number>, y: Iterable<number>): PowerFit;
entries.jsdocSummary: Power fit `y = a * x^b`, by least squares on `ln y` against `ln x`. `r2` is measured on the original y. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` unless every x and y is positive; `predict` needs a positive x.

entries.name: ProportionSampleSizeInput
entries.signature: export type ProportionSampleSizeInput = { marginOfError: number; proportion?: number; level?: number; stddev?: never; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Sample size for estimating a proportion; `proportion` defaults to 0.5, the worst case.

entries.name: quantile
entries.signature: export declare function quantile(values: Iterable<number>, q: number, options?: QuantileOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: The `q`-th quantile, `q` in `[0, 1]`, with the same methods as `percentile` (default R-7): `quantile(values, 0.9)` equals `percentile(values, 90)`. Throws `EmptyDataError` when empty and `InvalidArgumentError` when `q` is out of range.

entries.name: QUANTILE_METHODS
entries.signature: export declare const QUANTILE_METHODS: readonly ['inverseCdf', 'averagedInverseCdf', 'closestObservation', 'interpolatedInverseCdf', 'hazen', 'weibull', 'linear', 'medianUnbiased', 'normalUnbiased'];
entries.jsdocSummary: Hyndman & Fan's nine sample-quantile definitions (Amer. Statistician 50(4), 1996), by NumPy's names; R's `quantile(x, type = k)` is the R-k column.

entries.name: QuantileMethod
entries.signature: export type QuantileMethod = (typeof QUANTILE_METHODS)[number];

entries.name: QuantileOptions
entries.signature: export type QuantileOptions = { /** Sample-quantile definition; default `'linear'` (R-7). */ method?: QuantileMethod; };

entries.name: QuartileMethod
entries.signature: export type QuartileMethod = QuantileMethod | 'tukey' | 'medianExcluded';
entries.jsdocSummary: A quantile method, or one of the two "median of each half" rules. They differ only for an odd count, in where the middle value goes: - `'tukey'`: Tukey's hinges; the median belongs to BOTH halves (R `fivenum`, `boxplot.stats`; Wikipedia's "Method 2"). - `'medianExcluded'`: the median belongs to NEITHER half (TI-83/TI-84 `1-Var Stats`, Moore & McCabe; Wikipedia's "Method 1").

entries.name: QuartileOptions
entries.signature: export type QuartileOptions = { /** Default `'linear'` (R-7), like `quantile`. */ method?: QuartileMethod; };

entries.name: quartiles
entries.signature: export declare function quartiles(values: Iterable<number>, options?: QuartileOptions): Quartiles;
entries.jsdocSummary: The three quartiles in one sort. `method` is any `quantile` method (default `'linear'`, R-7), or a "median of each half" rule (see `QuartileMethod`): `'tukey'` (the box-plot hinges of R's `fivenum`, the middle value in both halves when the count is odd) or `'medianExcluded'` (the TI-83 rule, the middle value in neither half). A single value is all three quartiles. Throws `EmptyDataError` when empty.

entries.name: Quartiles
entries.signature: export type Quartiles = { /** First quartile (or lower hinge). */ q1: number; /** The median. */ q2: number; /** Third quartile (or upper hinge). */ q3: number; };

entries.name: sampleSize
entries.signature: export declare function sampleSize(input: MeanSampleSizeInput | ProportionSampleSizeInput): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Smallest sample size, rounded up, that keeps the margin of error at or below `marginOfError` with the given `level` (default 0.95), using the normal critical value `z`. For a mean pass `stddev`: `n = (z * stddev / E)^2`. For a proportion pass `proportion` (default 0.5, the worst case): `n = z^2 * p * (1 - p) / E^2`.

entries.name: SampleSummary
entries.signature: export type SampleSummary = { n: number; stddev: number; variance?: never; } | { n: number; variance: number; stddev?: never; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A group known only by its size and SAMPLE spread (ddof 1): `{ n, stddev }` or `{ n, variance }`. Accepted by `pooledVariance` and `pooledStddev`.

entries.name: standardError
entries.signature: export declare function standardError(values: Iterable<number> | { stddev: number; n: number; }, options?: VarianceOptions): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Standard error of the mean, `stddev / sqrt(n)`. Pass the data (its `stddev` uses `ddof`, sample by default) or a known `{ stddev, n }`. Throws `EmptyDataError` when the data has too few values.

entries.name: stddev
entries.signature: export declare function stddev(values: Iterable<number>, options?: VarianceOptions): number; ; export declare function stddev(values: Iterable<Decimal>, options: VarianceOptions & ScaleOptions): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Square root of `variance`, with the same `ddof` convention (sample by default). Square root of the exact variance, correctly rounded at the requested scale (default rounding `'halfEven'`). A square root rarely terminates, so `{ scale }` is required. The variance is kept as an exact fraction and the root is rounded once, so tiny variances and near-ties round correctly.

entries.name: sum
entries.signature: export declare function sum(values: Iterable<number>): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Total of the values using Neumaier compensated summation. An empty input gives `0`. Numbers only: for an exact total of `Decimal` values use `Decimal.sum`, which returns a `Decimal` zero for an empty input.

entries.name: variance
entries.signature: export declare function variance(values: Iterable<number>, options?: VarianceOptions): number; ; export declare function variance(values: Iterable<Decimal>, options?: VarianceOptions & Partial<ScaleOptions>): Decimal;
entries.jsdocSummary: Variance by the corrected two-pass algorithm. Sample (`ddof: 1`, divide by n - 1) by default; `ddof: 0` gives the population variance (divide by n). Throws `EmptyDataError` unless there are more than `ddof` values. Exact variance of `Decimal` values, computed as `(n * sum(x^2) - sum(x)^2) / (n * (n - ddof))` with a single division, so nothing is rounded before the end. Like `Decimal.dividedBy`, it throws `RoundingNecessaryError` when the result does not terminate unless you pass `{ scale, rounding }`.

entries.name: VarianceOptions
entries.signature: export type VarianceOptions = { /** Delta degrees of freedom: 1 = sample (default), 0 = population. */ ddof?: 0 | 1; };

entries.name: zScore
entries.signature: export declare function zScore(value: number, mean: number, stddev: number): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: How many standard deviations `value` lies from `mean`: `(value - mean) / stddev`. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` unless `stddev` is positive.

entries.name: convert
entries.signature: export declare function convert(value: number, from: Unit, to: Unit): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Converts `value` between two units of the same category, in doubles. `convert(1, 'in', 'cm')` is exactly `2.54`; `convert(100, 'C', 'F')` is `212`. Throws `InvalidArgumentError` for unknown units or units of different categories, and for `0` to or from `l/100km` (zero fuel use or zero distance per litre is infinite).

entries.name: convertExact
entries.signature: export declare function convertExact(value: RationalInput, from: Unit, to: Unit): Rational;
entries.jsdocSummary: Converts exactly, returning a `Rational`. Linear categories multiply by an exact ratio; temperature applies its exact affine formulas (`°F = °C × 9/5 + 32`, `K = °C + 273.15`); `l/100km` takes the exact reciprocal (`mpg` → `l/100km` is `100 / km-per-litre`).

entries.name: formatUnit
entries.signature: export declare function formatUnit(value: number, unit: Unit, options?: FormatUnitOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: Formats `value` with its unit through `Intl.NumberFormat`: `formatUnit(5, 'km')` is `'5 km'`, and with `{ display: 'long' }` it is `'5 kilometers'`. Units Intl has no name for (`nmi`, `psi`, `rad`, `K`, ...) print as the number, a space and the symbol; `display` does not apply to them. Power, frequency, force, torque, fuel economy and data rates all take this path (`Intl` names none of them), with `hp_metric` shown as `PS` and `N*m` as `N·m`.

entries.name: FormatUnitOptions
entries.signature: export type FormatUnitOptions = { /** BCP 47 locale; defaults to the runtime's. */ locale?: string; /** `'short'` (default) → `5 km`, `'long'` → `5 kilometers`, `'narrow'` → `5km`. */ display?: 'short' | 'long' | 'narrow'; maximumFractionDigits?: number; };

entries.name: joinUnits
entries.signature: export declare function joinUnits(parts: readonly UnitPart[], to: Unit): number;
entries.jsdocSummary: Adds composite parts back into one number in `to`: `joinUnits([{ unit: 'ft', value: 5 }, { unit: 'in', value: 7 }], 'in')` is `67`. Parts may come in any order and may be fractional. It reads parts the way `splitUnits` writes them: the sign of the first non-zero part applies to the whole value, so `-5 ft 7 in` is minus (5 ft + 7 in), `-67 in`. Later parts must not be negative (`InvalidArgumentError`); that would be ambiguous. The sum is exact, rounded to a double once at the end.

entries.name: splitUnits
entries.signature: export declare function splitUnits(value: RationalInput, from: Unit, units: readonly Unit[], options?: SplitUnitsOptions): UnitPart[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Splits a value into whole parts of larger units plus a remainder, for display like "5 ft 7 in", "1 h 30 min" or "3 lb 4 oz". `units` go largest first and share one category: `splitUnits(67, 'in', ['ft', 'in'])` is `[{ unit: 'ft', value: 5 }, { unit: 'in', value: 7 }]`.

entries.name: SplitUnitsOptions
entries.signature: export type SplitUnitsOptions = { /** * Fraction digits kept on the last part. Leave it out to keep the exact remainder * (as a double). The value is rounded once, in the last unit, before it is split, * so a rounded-up remainder carries into the larger parts: 5 ft 11.6 in at * `scale: 0` is 6 ft 0 in, never 5 ft 12 in. */ scale?: number; /** How to round to `scale`. Defaults to `'halfUp'`. Ignored without `scale`. */ rounding?: RoundingMode; };

entries.signature: export declare const en: NumberWordsLocale;

entries.signature: export type Gender = 'masculine' | 'feminine' | 'neuter';

entries.name: NumberWordsLocale
entries.signature: export type NumberWordsLocale = { /** BCP 47 tag, also used for digit formatting. */ readonly code: string; /** The word placed before a negative number: `minus`. */ readonly negative: string; /** The word read for the decimal separator: `point`, `virgulă`, `Komma`. */ readonly decimalSeparator: string; /** * How many base-1000 groups the locale can spell (`en`: 12, up to 10^36 − 1). * The core rejects longer integers with `NumericRangeError` by digit count, * before any grouping work is done. */ readonly maxGroups: number; /** Cardinal words for `n ≥ 0`. Throws `NumericRangeError` beyond the locale's largest scale word. */ spell(n: bigint, context: WordsContext): string; /** Ordinal words for `n ≥ 1`: `twenty-first`, `al douăzeci și unulea`. */ spellOrdinal(n: bigint, context: WordsContext): string; /** Ordinal with digits for `n ≥ 1`: `21st`, `21.`, `al 21-lea`. `digits` is `n` already formatted for the locale. */ ordinal(n: bigint, digits: string, context: WordsContext): string; };
entries.jsdocSummary: The contract a locale implements. All inputs are non-negative integers; the core handles sign, fractions and thresholds.

entries.name: OrdinalOptions
entries.signature: export type OrdinalOptions = { locale?: NumberWordsLocale; gender?: Gender; };

entries.name: spellNumber
entries.signature: export declare function spellNumber(value: DecimalInput, options?: SpellOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: `spellNumber(102)` → `'one hundred two'`; `spellNumber('3.14')` → `'three point one four'`; `spellNumber(-5)` → `'minus five'`. Fractions are read digit by digit, as people do. Numbers are read through `decimal()`, so `0.1` is "zero point one", never its binary expansion.

entries.name: SpellOptions
entries.signature: export type SpellOptions = { locale?: NumberWordsLocale; gender?: Gender; /** * Numbers are spelled when `after < |value| ≤ until`; the rest come back as * formatted digits that keep the exact value (every fraction digit is kept). * `until` is the inclusive upper bound of the spelled range. */ until?: number; /** The exclusive lower bound of the spelled range (see `until`). */ after?: number; };

entries.name: spellOrdinal
entries.signature: export declare function spellOrdinal(value: DecimalInput, options?: OrdinalOptions): string;
entries.jsdocSummary: `spellOrdinal(21)` → `'twenty-first'`. Positive integers only.

entries.name: thousandsGroups
entries.signature: export declare function thousandsGroups(n: bigint): number[];
entries.jsdocSummary: Splits a non-negative integer into base-1000 groups, most significant first: `1234567n` → `[1, 234, 567]`. The building block every locale uses.

entries.name: WordsContext
entries.signature: export type WordsContext = { /** Grammatical gender of the thing being counted, where the language cares (`una`/`unu`, `première`/`premier`). */ gender: Gender | undefined; };
